findings.title: Rejected devices are cached in localCache before DB check, bypassing the device limit on subsequent requests
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is called on line 87 before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` on line 93. When the device limit has been reached, the first request from a new device fails with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, but its device key is already stored in `localCache` for 29 minutes. On the very next request from that same device (including follow-up requests during the same page load), `a.localCache.Get(key)` on line 83 succeeds and `tagDeviceUI` returns `nil` without querying the store, allowing `Anonymous.Authenticate` to succeed and bypassing the device limit. `localCache.SetDefault` should only be called after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds (and `untagDevice` should also evict the key from `localCache` when deleting a device).

findings.title: Provider signature changes in ProvideAnonymousDeviceService and ProvideAnonDBStore break Wire DI compilation
findings.body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` was changed from accepting `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` to `sqlStore db.DB`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` was changed to take `(sqlStore db.DB, deviceLimit int64)`. However, the Wire dependency injection files (`pkg/server/wire.go` and `pkg/server/wire_gen.go`, as well as any other wire sets referencing these providers) were not updated in this PR, which will cause `pkg/server` compilation and `wire` generation to fail.

findings.title: updateDevice relies on RowsAffected() == 0, which falsely rejects existing devices on MySQL when values are unchanged
findings.body: In `updateDevice`, `rowsAffected == 0` is used to infer that the device was not found in `anon_device`, returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. On MySQL (where `clientFoundRows` is disabled by default and `DATETIME` columns have 1-second precision), `UPDATE` reports 0 rows affected if a row matches the `WHERE` clause but `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `updated_at` (within the same second) do not change. When an already-registered device makes concurrent requests within the same second (or across multiple Grafana replicas that do not share `localCache`), `RowsAffected()` will return 0 on MySQL and wrongly fail with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

findings.title: GrafanaBootConfig.anonymousDeviceLimit is inferred as type undefined instead of number | undefined
findings.body: In `GrafanaBootConfig`, `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` is declared without an explicit type annotation (unlike `loginError: string | undefined = undefined;` on line 85 or optional properties using `?:`). Because the exported `config` singleton in `@grafana/runtime` is typed as `GrafanaBootConfig`, TypeScript infers `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` as having type `undefined` rather than `number | undefined`, preventing callers from treating it as a `number`. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` or `anonymousDeviceLimit?: number;`.
